memory_candidates.content: An audit or inventory artifact can be stale by construction: check its commit time against the commit times of the changes it enumerates before planning from it. A census committed after the deletions it lists as 'surviving' describes a snapshot that no longer exists, and planning from it manufactures work that is already done. The countermeasure is a name-anchored census against the live tree as a mandatory first phase, gating all writes, with a hard stop rather than ad hoc re-derivation if the census diverges. Anchor such censuses on declaration names, never line numbers -- line numbers drift on every refactor. A corollary for exclusion records: a documented 'reasoned exclusion' can be falsified by a later unrelated change to the excluded item's origin (e.g. a signature acquiring an omit prefix), so re-verify an exclusion's stated evidence rather than inheriting its verdict.
